title:
Space engineering
Communications
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Section (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-50C Revision Working Group)
status_notes: Second issue, Revision 2, dated 5 December 2024. It revises ECSS-E-ST-50C Rev.1 (1 March 2021), which revised ECSS-E-ST-50C (31 July 2008), itself following ECSS-E-50 Part 1A (20 October 2003) and Part 2A (4 July 2005); ECSS-E-ST-50B was never issued (change log, p. 3). Whether a later revision exists is not stated in the document.

contents.title: Terms specific to the present standard
Communication system architectural design document (CSADD) - DRD (normative)
Communication system detailed design document (CSDDD) - DRD (normative)

key_points.text: Rev.2 removes the issue identifier and date of the adopted CCSDS documents, so that ECSS-E-ST-50 does not need updating whenever an adopted CCSDS standard is updated; it also deletes 12 terms from clause 3.2 (communication service, cross support, downlink, service-provider, service-user, sink, telecommand, telemetry, telemetry link, uplink, user, user application).

The standard covers space-ground and space-to-space links in operations and the links used in AIT; it details the space link and space network domains and covers only the ground network aspects needed for end-to-end services (others are in ECSS-E-ST-70).

For control operations the objective is guaranteed delivery of commands in transmission order (commands can be repeated but not lost); for payload data the aim is to transfer as much data as possible, accepting some loss.

Table in clause 4.2: ECSS-E-AS-50-21 (CCSDS 131.0-B) supersedes the whole of ECSS-E-ST-50-01C; -22 (132.0-B) the TM Transfer Frame of ECSS-E-ST-50-03C; -23 (732.0-B) adds AOS; -24 (231.0-B), -25 (232.0-B) and -26 (232.1-B) replace clauses 8-9, 5-6 and 7 of ECSS-E-ST-50-04C.

Figure 4-2 maps CCSDS and Internet protocols onto the data link, coding and physical layers and upper layers, marks which CCSDS books are formally adopted by ECSS, and gives ECSS-E-ST-70-41C as an example of an application-specific source/sink.
Communication engineering milestones include SRR, PDR, CDR, QR, AR, ORR and FRR.

Requirement 5.4.2 demands a service guaranteeing in-sequence delivery of telecommands; 5.4.3 requires the probability of accepting an erroneous telecommand to be below 10^-2/N, N being the number of telecommands expected over the mission.

Essential telecommands must be decodable and distributed even when all other systems, including the CDMU, are non-operational; their list is agreed at PDR and, for critical operations, they must not depend on software.
Telecommand encryption is required when authentication alone cannot meet the security requirements; the SDLS option of ECSS-E-AS-50-25 is cited as a data-link-layer means.

Hot-redundant TC chains must not repeatedly select the input channel with lower signal quality (dual-lock issue, ECSS-E-HB-50 clause 4.4.5.2), and all telecommands must carry a destination spacecraft identifier.
Uplink budgets are based on a BER of 10^-5 at the telecommand decoder input; at that BER the uplink frame rejection rate for 256-octet frames shall be below 10^-5.

Downlink frame rejection should be below 10^-5 and the probability of accepting corrupted maximum-sized downlink frames below 10^-12; with BCH, undetected uplink frame error can be below 10^-18 with frame error control and 10^-8 without.
An application for frequency assignment shall be made to the Radio Communication Bureau of the ITU for the selected space communication frequencies.
Formatted space link data units shall carry a sequence identifier giving their position in the stream (5.6.13.3), and the space link protocol shall include an error detection capability (5.6.13.4).
The space link shall provide a guaranteed delivery service and an expedited delivery service for SDUs (5.6.14.2, 5.6.14.3).
The space link provides telecommand receipt confirmation and exception reporting; ranging/Doppler methods are referred to ECSS-E-ST-50-02.

The CSPD (Annex G) is the supplier's formal statement of compliance with ECSS-E-ST-50, listing frequencies, protocols and options, address, channel and spacecraft identifier assignments and bandwidth allocations; first version at CDR, final at FRR.

notes: Newer revision of the library item ecss-e-st-50c-rev-1-1march2021 (Rev.1, 1 March 2021). Apart from the changes listed in the change log, the text is essentially that of Rev.1, but pagination shifts by one page from clause 4 onwards because clause 3.2 is shorter (for example clause 4 starts on p. 15 here, p. 16 in Rev.1). The change log entry for Rev.1 is reduced to a lone bullet (p. 3), and the Rev.2 entry contains 'to avoid a an update' (p. 3). The foreword omits the sentence about the series of ECSS standards. Clause 3.3 still cites 'ECSS-ST-00-01' (p. 13). Figure 4-2 is a diagram whose labels are extracted as jumbled text (p. 20); its note still contains 'axample' and still names 'ECSS-E-50-05' for RF and modulation. Clause 4.3.2 is still headed 'Space network'. The 'mentioned' entries come from the clause 4.2 table, Figure 4-2 and running text, not from a reference list. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; srcgrep shows 89 PDF pages (the last one blank) while the registry gives 88.
